html:
Mirabai was a Rajput princess of the 16th century who gave up court life for the love of the god Krishna. Her songs are among the best known in India.

Almost everything about her comes from stories written down later. She was born about 1498 into the ruling family of Merta in Rajasthan. In 1516 she was married to the heir of Mewar, the leading Rajput kingdom. He died within a few years.

Mira said her true husband was Krishna. She refused to live as a silent widow, sang and danced in temples and kept company with wandering holy men of any caste. Her husband's family were shamed. The stories say they sent her a cup of poison, which turned to nectar, and a snake in a basket, which became a garland. She left Mewar, lived as a pilgrim at Vrindavan and died at Dwarka in Gujarat about 1547. Legend says she walked into Krishna's image and vanished.

Hundreds of songs carry her name, in Rajasthani and Braj Hindi. Many were added by later singers. They speak in a woman's voice of longing for the "dark one" and of giving up family honour. She belongs to the bhakti movement. Gandhi held her up as a model of resistance without violence.
